Name: Stand
Description En: A central glass-walled kitchen is the focal point of this eye-catching modern restaurant; a dining room sits either side, and there’s a chatty buzz to the room, which is helped along by the personable service team. The two experienced chef-owners are proud of their Hungarian roots and skilfully reinvent and modernise classic Hungarian dishes using a wide range of techniques. The wonderfully rich gulyás soup and the soft, flavoursome venison are hits, as is the ever-present somlói dessert. When it comes to wine, look to the Hungarian options – there are some great sweet Tokajis on the list.

Name: Platán Gourmet
Address: Platán Manor, Kastély tér 6, Tata, 2890, Hungary
Description En: Your evening starts with an aperitif and snacks at the Chef's Table, before you are shown through to a barrel-vaulted cellar with an open kitchen. Here, the team work with calm efficiency and meticulous precision to create a 12 course tasting menu composed of highly sophisticated dishes packed with deep, well-balanced flavours and bags of personality. The setting beneath the castle is magical; for the full experience, stay the night in one of the nearby bedrooms and make the most of their spa.

Name: Costes
Description En: Elegance and sophistication lead the way at Costes, from the smart décor to the well-orchestrated service. Ask for a seat to the front of the main room for a feeling of space, then enjoy the eager anticipation as the sommelier presents an exceptional, mostly Hungarian wine selection. The modern 7 course tasting menu comprises memorable dishes which not only look stunning with their bright colours and artistic style, but are packed with vibrant, complementary flavours. Seasonality plays an important role here too, with the featured ingredients always informing you of what’s in season right now.

Name: Babel
Description En: A city institution, Babel represents the perfect blend of tradition and modernity. Its walls still show marks from the 1838 Great Flood of Pest, yet it’s also a chic, stylish place thanks to passionate owner Hubert and interior designer Annamaria Dekany. The cooking follows in a similar vein, with the multi-course tasting menu comprising consummately seasoned, creative modern dishes which simultaneously exhibit references to their Hungarian heritage. Highlights include red shrimp with tomato and plankton, and guinea fowl with a steamed bun; be sure to go for the casino egg ‘add-on’ too.

Name: Salt
Address: Hotel Rum Budapest, Királyi Pál utca 4, Budapest, 1053, Hungary
Description En: Within a boutique hotel sits this small, sophisticated restaurant, whose open kitchen forms an integral part of the stylishly lit room. Shelves are full of jars containing colourfully preserved foraged fruits, vegetables and herbs, and the butter, lardo and Mangalitsa ham are all produced in-house. The surprise set menu is made up of intricate, exquisitely constructed dishes – many of which are updated versions of classic Hungarian recipes – and tables all face the wood-clad ‘pass’, where the chefs assemble the dishes in front of your eyes with skill and dexterity.

Name: Pajta
Description En: Pajta means ‘barn’, which is where it all began for Flóra and Ferenc – in the small barn beside this glass-fronted restaurant. The whole complex has a natural feel, from the beautiful meadow to the two-storey, nature-inspired forest lodges 1km down the road (they arrange transportation). Menus change with the seasons and perfectly reflect the area, championing produce from Őrség in historical Hungarian dishes. Fermenting and pickling are a feature, adding a welcome punch to the flavour-packed creations. Neighbouring Austria and Slovenia join Hungary for a tri-country wine pairing experience.

Name: Rumour by Rácz Jenő
Description En: After travelling the world, Chef Jenő returned home to open this unique restaurant. Located in the heart of the city, it comes with concrete walls hung with mirrors, and a 21-seater counter which wraps around the large open kitchen. Red leather stools and placemats provide colour, while a trendy soundtrack adds to the vibe. The set menu showcases elements from Jenő’s travels via a series of refined, creative, sometimes playful dishes that burst with flavour. These are matched by some serious wine pairings, with the Hungarian option offering some wonderfully unique, bespoke choices.

Name: essência
Description En: Portuguese Chef-Owner Tiago and his Hungarian wife Éva have created a warmly run and deliciously different restaurant in the heart of the city. A bright front room with arched windows leads past the open kitchen to a more intimate room where patches of blue and white tiling hint at Tiago’s heritage. At dinner, pick from 5 or 7 courses – some have choices, allowing you to lead with either Portuguese or Hungarian influences, or to combine them for the best of both worlds. The interesting, flavour-packed dishes are poised and elegant, and Tiago has a deft touch when it comes to seasoning.

A pastel blue townhouse plays host to this series of intimate, elegant dining rooms, but many favour a spot in the striking glass-enclosed terrace overlooking the street. The multi-course menu opens with dishes inspired by the chef’s global travels, before moving on to offer refined versions of more local recipes. Beautifully presented, wonderfully flavoured Hungarian produce might include Danube salmon – accompanied by caviar, butter sauce and dill – or aged Mangalitsa ham with white asparagus, morels and chervil. Charming service and an impressive wine cellar add to the experience, as do the luxurious bedrooms.

Name: Borkonyha Winekitchen
Description En: While it would be easy to do, to pass by this unassuming-looking restaurant near the Basilica would be a mistake. The kitchen here sources top-class ingredients, treats them with the utmost respect and allows them to shine. Subtle Hungarian influences run throughout dishes which are well-conceived, skilfully executed and have a notable intensity of flavour. There is an à la carte, but go for the tasting menu for the best experience. Wines are key here too: they offer 100 labels, including some of Hungary’s top producers, with many available by the glass.

Name: Anyukám Mondta
Description En: Anyukám Mondta is everything a good neighbourhood restaurant should be. It offers something to appeal to everyone, while prices cover a wide range to suit all occasions. Excellent produce is prepared with care, resulting in hearty, flavoursome dishes, and service is smooth, well-paced and comes with plenty of personality. Choose from homemade pizzas, refined modern Italian dishes and tempting daily specials – where you might find some Middle Eastern flavours too. The focaccia cooked in the wood-fired oven is a must.

Name: Platán Bisztró
Address: Platán Manor, Kastély tér 6, Tata, 2890, Hungary
Description En: Part of the Platán complex – which also includes a hotel and spa – this charming bistro sits within the same historic castle outbuilding as Two Michelin Starred Platán Gourmet. It has a pleasingly relaxed, contemporary style, and in the corner is a small shop selling desserts and ice cream. In summer you can dine beneath the branches of a 230-year-old sycamore tree on a charming stepped terrace which borders the lake. The concise menu sees robust Hungarian dishes given a refined bistro-style makeover while still staying true to their roots. Service is fittingly warm and chatty.

Name: Macok Bistro
Description En: Set on a cobbled street in the Old Town, alongside the castle walls, this bright, colourful bistro is known by food-lovers across the country – and it certainly deserves its reputation. It’s family-owned and professionally run by a friendly team, and the menu is an appealing mix of colourful Hungarian and Mediterranean dishes. While classic flavours are in abundance, presentation is decidedly modern; the wild boar soup is not to be missed, as is the beef cheek goulash. As well as a wine shop, they also have bedrooms, and in summer you can sit in the courtyard beside the working water wheel.

Name: Sparhelt
Description En: Head away from the lakeside to seek out this honest all-day bistro with a smart modern interior and a popular terrace. Dishes have a Hungarian heart and perfectly reflect the seasons, with the likes of chilled fruit soups in summer and hearty, warming dishes in winter. Meat-lovers should order the mangalitsa Wellington if they see it on the menu, while fish fanatics should come on Fridays for the special seafood menu. They offer wines from around the world, but don't pass up the opportunity to try some of the superb local Lake Balaton options.

Name: Casa Christa
Description En: Roads fringed by almond trees and terraced vines lead to this stunning hillside spot; a restful place that comes with seven restored press houses that now play host to designer bedrooms with private saunas. Within the grounds sits this beautiful whitewashed restaurant with a simple bistro-cum-farmhouse style and a lovely terrace affording far-reaching views over the countryside towards Lake Balaton. The generous cooking has a similarly Mediterranean feel, with bright colours and bold, contrasting flavours – expect the likes of lamb soup with sour cream, followed by chicken with pea risotto.

Name: Cabrio
Description En: Tucked away in the city centre on a small square, Cabrio’s tree-shaded terrace is the perfect place to kick back with a glass of wine. A 100% natural wine bar, it offers generously priced bottles from both Hungary and across Europe, and comes with a vintage look and a trendy vibe. The friendly team are keen to offer recommendations when it comes to both the wine and the concise selection of seasonal small plates (three per person is about right). Boldly flavoured, well-judged combinations could include burnt celeriac carpaccio, salmon trout tartare with green gazpacho or raspberry chocolate crémeux cake.

Name: Goli
Description En: Set within the former Goldberger textile factory, Goli refers to the nickname the locals gave to this historic building. It’s a small place with a simple terrace and a colourful, cramped interior, but it’s gloriously friendly and positive vibes simply pour out of the kitchen. Sit at the counter to talk with the chefs, who are eager to guide you through the menu of fresh, tasty Middle Eastern favourites, from warm pita, vibrant salads, and green beans with chilli and lemon, to charred entrecôte with tahini. Deliciously fruity soft drinks and cocktails complete your meal.

Name: Iszkor
Description En: This lovely neighbourhood restaurant sits in a small village in the Bükk Mountains and is run by charming couple Adam and Luca. It couldn’t be a bigger part of the community. Not only does it reside in Adam’s home village, but the locals get involved by growing produce for them – and that's without considering the host of events on offer, from live music and guest chef evenings to seasonal Farmers' Markets. The generously proportioned, country-style dishes change with the seasons and use every part of the ingredient. In summer, sit on the decked terrace; in winter, cosy up beside the fire.

Name: N28 Wine and Kitchen
Description En: You’ll be greeted as if you’re a regular diner here, even on your first visit, which immediately sets a cheerful tone. The welcoming team come, in part, from the Bock Bistzró stable – and they know how to look after their guests. The surroundings might be modern, but there’s a traditional element to the menu, which looks to the Hungarian larder for its base. Expect seasonally changing dishes such as a tasty vichyssoise soup, followed by juicy wild boar and then a delicious poppy seed cake. 95% of the wines are Hungarian, and everything comes at a great price.

Name: Morzsa
Description En: ‘Crumbs’ is a new wave bakery-cum-bistro with a relaxed urban style, owned by a charismatic and exuberant designer. Sit inside to watch the making of the delicious loaves and pastries or head out to the terrace for some people-watching in the part-pedestrianised lane. Modern, flavour-packed small plates are served throughout the day and can be accompanied by something from the biodynamic wine list. Naturally, a pastry is a must to finish, but with so many delicious options it can be hard to choose... and if you simply can't decide, there's always the option to take something home for later too!

Name: Kistücsök
Description En: A short walk from the southern shores of Lake Balaton, Kistücsök is part of a small hotel which comes complete with its own swimming pool. Well-regarded locally, the restaurant is known for its consistently good interpretations of classic Hungarian dishes, which have been modernised both in their composition and their look. Flavours are fresh, with the occasional global influence, and prices are reasonable. The ‘Taste of the Region’ menu with wine pairings is always a great choice, and the floating island dessert has become something of a speciality.

Name: Újváros Bisztró
Description En: If you’re in eastern Hungary, it’s worth heading over to this ultra-modern restaurant on the banks of the Holt-Körös River. It occupies a space on the ground floor of a modern office building and is accessed via steps that lead to the river path, where you’ll also find the charming terrace with views of Bolza Castle. Choose between three tasting menus: ‘From Here’ (built around local ingredients), ‘From There’ (reinterpreted Hungarian recipes) and ‘From Everywhere’ (dishes with international flavours). An interesting selection of Hungarian wines accompanies, arranged on the list by region.

Name: 94' Konyha & Bar
Description En: It might have changed location, but a warm welcome and great value food awaits at 94' Konyha & Bar. The super-fresh, vibrantly flavoured cooking has a clear Vietnamese heart, with dishes including a tasty pho and creations such as their own 94' Gohan – a blend of beef, fried rice and XO sauce – but you’ll find some other Asian flavours at play here too. The ‘Lunch Break’ menu is a particular steal and always be sure to finish with a Vietnamese coffee, you won't regret it.

Name: Majorelle
Description En: Named after the vibrant botanical garden in Marrakesh, this Moroccan restaurant, set in an impressive five-storey building boasting a balconied frontage, certainly won’t disappoint. All the Moroccan greats are here, from pastilla and briouats to zaalouk and tajines, and Chef Saad imports his spices directly, so his dishes burst with authentic combinations of spicy and sweet. Sharing is a given, but maybe not when it comes to the delicious jawhara (crisp layered pastry filled with orange blossom cream). The fresh mint tea is a must-try, delivered by a warm, friendly team.

Name: Dereszla Bisztró
Description En: There are few places more relaxing to dine than on the stepped riverside terrace of this modern wood and glass building located in the heart of wine country. Szabó and his front-of-house team warmly welcome you in, while his brother Bém works behind the scenes in the kitchen preparing a concise menu of modern Hungarian dishes. Good quality produce comes from their carefully selected suppliers, whether that’s local Mangalitsa or trout from Lillafüred, which could arrive served ‘kárpáti’ style with a creamy fish bone sauce. Considering the location, a Tokaj wine is the natural accompaniment.

Name: Víg Molnár Csárda
Description En: This traditional-looking tavern comes with plenty of character and is certainly a hit with the locals. There’s a rustic, slightly Mediterranean feel to the décor, which works well with its location near the lake, but the best place to sit is on the large terrace beside the working water wheel. Fairly priced, hearty Hungarian classics are the order of the day, with the meat-stuffed pancakes a speciality. Children have their own menu too, and you’ll be well looked after by the friendly owners and their team. It’s a place for every occasion, so can get very busy at peak times.

Name: Padi
Description En: If wine’s your thing, you can’t go wrong with a visit to this striking hillside building in the heart of wine country. You must open, of course, with one of their own Sauska wines in the smart bar, before heading through to the sleek restaurant whose wonderful terrace offers views over the vines below. There’s a small à la carte of refined, eye-catching dishes as well as two tasting menus on offer, one themed around Tokaj itself – choose this option along with their local wine recommendations to fully immerse yourself in the region. To really complete the experience, ask for a peek into their winery below.

Name: Végállomás Bistro&Wine
Description En: It might be tucked away in the suburbs, but this neighbourhood bistro is so highly regarded that plenty of people come from further afield. The cosy terrace has its own wooden bar, and the split-level interior has a relaxed, traditional feel. The ever-evolving menu of seasonal dishes offers something for everyone, and the lunchtime options are great value; keep an eye out for the Bird’s milk and orange egg white foam dessert.

Name: Tiszavirág
Description En: A recently restored Victorian townhouse that was formerly home to a goldsmith’s now plays host to this smart restaurant. Start with a drink in the cosy bar before enjoying boldly flavoured dishes that come with a refined look but a traditional Hungarian heart, such as Mangalitsa fillet with gnudi and cottage cheese. In warmer weather, these are best enjoyed in the enclosed courtyard, along with a bottle or two from the proudly Hungarian wine list. Service is smooth and eager to please, and comes together with elegant bedrooms and a mini spa in the basement to help create a charming picture.

Name: Csopaki Resti
Description En: There’s no denying that a meal at Csopaki Resti provides something a little different, as this tiny restaurant comprises just six seats and sits within the old village railway station. Because of its compact size, every diner can watch the chefs preparing the dishes in the on-view kitchen, but the four counter seats are undeniably the best place to be; wherever you sit, the chefs will serve you personally. The multi-course set menu takes on a refreshingly modern approach, while still keeping traditional Hungarian flavours to the fore.

Name: Szaletly
Description En: Whether you’re after a drink, a snack or a full meal, this neighbourhood spot is for you if you’re after a laid-back vibe. It’s a spacious place, with a large terrace-cum-garden to boot, but the efficient team cope well with the numbers. Dishes offer a diverse range of influences, but there’s always a Hungarian vein running through their hearts. The tasting menus with matching wines are worth ordering, the gödöllő chicken breast is delicious and, for dessert, it has to be the esterházy. You can even buy a post-dessert ice cream for the way home.

Name: Natura Hill
Description En: It’s all in the name at this sustainably led restaurant. The climb up the steep, narrow lane to the two-hectare estate results in breathtaking Danube Bend views, which become all the more special at sunset. The kitchen follows a ‘slow food’ ethos; ingredients from their nearby farm and the local area underpin the cooking, and menus evolve twice a day as new produce arrives. Dishes are fresh, unfussy and vibrantly flavoured – come for the ‘Spontaneous Bistro Lunch’ or the tasting menu at dinner. An overnight stay is a must, with the holistic experience also including a sauna and wellness centre.

Name: Fausto's
Description En: The super-elegant Fausto’s might not have been open in this location all that long, but it’s owner, Chef Fausto Di Vora, can proudly claim over 30 successful years in the city. Following a move from Pest to Buda, his rebirthed restaurant remains as personally and professionally run as ever, but now with an added vigour. The glass-enclosed terrace is a great spot to enjoy Italian dishes such as shrimps with butternut squash and vegetable vinaigrette, whose presentation is a match for the wonderful surroundings. This is certainly a place to sit back, relax and let la dolce vita run through your soul.

Name: Spago by Wolfgang Puck
Address: Matild Palace Hotel, Váci utca 36, Budapest, 1056, Hungary
Description En: The Matild Palace Hotel – one of a pair of matching belle époque palaces bult by the Archduchess of Austria – is a grand building in a stunning setting beside the Elizabeth Bridge. It’s fitting then, that it’s home to a smart restaurant run by an Austrian Chef. Wolfgang Puck’s fun dining concept brings something a little different to Budapest’s culinary scene, with a selection of appealing, well-executed dishes that draw their inspiration from across the world. From Hungarian buffalo steak tartare and Austrian wiener schnitzel to scallop pad thai and some delicious pastas, everything is here.

Name: Sauska 48
Description En: Find a table on the spacious terrace of this modern winery to enjoy wonderful views out across the vineyard and the hills; on a warm summer’s day, it doesn’t get much better than this. The well-curated wine list covers Hungary and Europe, and includes reds and rosés from the vines you see in front of you, as well as whites from the owners’ other winery in Tokaj. The concise selection of contemporary dishes take their inspiration from the Hungarian kitchen but exhibit a level of refined creativity. The passionate team will share their knowledge to help you find the perfect wine match.

Name: UMO
Address: Monastery Boutique Hotel Budapest, Ponty utca 1, Budapest, 1011, Hungary
Description En: Housed within a boutique hotel, Umo comprises two parts: a contemporary brasserie in the atrium, and an enclosed courtyard towards the back of the building. The latter was formerly a monastery and is a wonderful place to sit – it even comes complete with an open kitchen where dishes are cooked over flames and smoke. Menus showcase the best of Latin American flavours, with everything from ceviches and a baja shrimp cocktail to a selection of fire-cooked meats and some delicious churros. A fine range of gins is on offer alongside the in-depth wine list, and the super-friendly team bring the whole experience together.

Name: Zelna Borbisztró
Description En: A smart, modern wine bar in the livelier part of this seasonal town, Zelna is named after the wine company whose biodynamic wines it serves – and also offers for purchase. This is a place to kick back and relax, and the small menu mixes light bites with more substantial Hungarian dishes so you can tailor-make your own experience – the beef cheeks are a hit and be sure to save room for the golden walnut dumplings for dessert! Every table is located on the large terrace, which stays open until 2am.

Name: Petrányi Csopak
Description En: If you’re looking to immerse yourself in a traditional Hungarian experience, then head straight for Petrányi Csopak. Perched high on the hillside, this period house sits within the sloping Petrányi Pince vineyard and affords lovely views out over the countryside and towards Lake Balaton in the middle distance. The menu offers a range of dishes that are inspired by the traditional home-cooked meals of the past – the kind of dishes that most Hungarian households have their own family recipes for, such as soups, stews and ragouts. The salmon trout with leek, potato, béchamel and lemon is a great way to start.

Name: Alelí
Address: Dorothea Hotel, Wekerle Sándor utca 3, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description En: Romance is in the air at this elegant, high-ceilinged restaurant inside the Dorothea Hotel in the heart of Budapest. Start with a classic cocktail in the chic bar, then move on to Italian favourites, from delicious focaccias and salads dressed at the table to freshly made pizzas, pastas and risottos. The spaghetti cacio e pepe is not to be missed, and the tiramisu is large enough to share. Much of the produce is imported from Italy and the authentic flavours shine through. Service is friendly and professional, with the staff keen to recommend both dishes and wines.

Name: Cut & Barrel
Description En: Set away from the city centre in the old Goldberger textile factory, this lovely warehouse conversion comprises a wine shop, an impressive bar, a large dining room with a terrace and a smaller anteroom offering counter dining. The stunning shop comes complete with an incredible selection of wines from around the country – including from the owner’s vineyard (Haraszthy Wines in Etyek) – as well as a Harley Davidson, a Porsche and a Rolls Royce. The food has a strong Latin American base but it’s their own charcuterie and succulent steaks from the Josper grill that lead the way.

Name: LAMAREDA
Description En: Located in the pedestrianised streets of the beautiful baroque city of Győr, this long-standing restaurant fits in perfectly thanks to its traditional, low-key elegance. Head past the bistro area at the front to the bright room behind, where they serve a menu which mixes Hungarian, Mediterranean and even some subtle Thai influences. The bright, vibrant dishes come in generous portions, with well-judged flavours – be sure to save room for a comforting dessert such as the gundel or zsabo pancakes. The smart pavement terrace is a hit come summer.

Name: Hosszú Tányér
Description En: This romantic little restaurant sits in an attractive courtyard setting and is keenly run by its hands-on owner Franciska. Nothing is too much trouble for her when it comes to her guests, who she encourages to relax and fully appreciate the experience. The five-course tasting menu comes with plenty of little extras and the flavour-packed dishes are truly beautiful to look at – with flavours to match. In an all-encompassing experience, the contemporary artwork on the walls changes every two months along with the menu – and the ceramic dishes are specially designed by the chef himself.

Name: MÁK by Mizsseyani
Description En: Rustic charm abounds at this laid-back restaurant, from the décor to the vaulted brick ceiling. Seasonality is key here and Chef János takes time to visit his small, artisan suppliers personally. His travels inform the interesting set menu (go for the longer version), with vegetables treated as reverently as meat and fish, and curing, pickling and ageing all playing their part. Knowledgably prepared, consummately seasoned dishes have a delicate touch and could include grey catfish with buckwheat or duck with celery and pine. The unobtrusive, expertly paced service is spot-on too.

Name: BiBo Budapest
Address: Dorothea Hotel, Apáczai Csere János utca 11, 7th Floor, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description En: Take the dedicated lift up to the seventh floor of the Dorothea Hotel and you’ll be warmly greeted with magical views across the river towards Budapest Castle. Start with one of their signature cocktails on the terrace to take it all in, then choose from a menu that fuses Hungary and Spain with aplomb. From rock prawn tempura to their signature ‘Garcia’ burgers or chicken stuffed with morels – as well as dishes to share – everything is generously proportioned and expertly delivered. Providing a perfect match is a wine list that favours, you may have guessed it, Hungary and Spain.

Name: Bilanx
Description En: Located in an old townhouse midway between the Széchenyi Chain Bridge and St. Stephen's Basilica, Bilanx takes a fresh, modern approach to dining out. Its interior is sparsely decorated, with varnished wooden chairs set at white-tile-topped tables, while neon light strips create glowing archways above and pop music plays through the speakers. The chef offers a tasting menu which combines his two loves – Hungarian produce and classical French techniques, so you’ll find dishes like Mangalitsa pork with choron sauce and parsley root cream. There’s also an interesting three-course menu available at lunch.

Name: Arany Kaviár
Description En: As its name implies, caviar plays a starring role here, with a range of almost 20 Hungarian and Siberian options on offer, as well as two different caviar tasting experiences. French and Russian influences guide the cooking, with the à la carte featuring a selection of dishes which have appeared on the menu since their opening under the heading 'Since 1990', and the tasting menu showcasing the chef's favourite creations. Sit in the opulent, richly appointed dining room or the more modern extension which opens out onto the garden – or book the Chef’s Table to really get in on the action.

Name: Alkimista Kulináris Műhely
Description En: Its name means ‘Culinary Workshop’ but that feels like doing it an injustice, as this is a beautiful, elegant spot. It's hidden away behind locked gates in a city centre courtyard and everyone is greeted at 7pm by the infectiously enthusiastic chef-owner. Seasonal ingredients feature on a highly personalised tasting menu which cleverly blends the old and the new. Flavours are memorable, sauces are a highlight and the chef describes every dish with heartfelt passion. The price also includes a carefully curated selection of drinks featuring many local biodynamic and organic wines.

Name: Zincenco Kitchen
Description En: Offering something a little different, this restaurant is located within a residential apartment, but there’s certainly nothing amateurish or domestic about it; it's even licensed. There are six tables – for a maximum of 14 diners – and all guests are asked to arrive at 7pm, which helps contribute to the supper party atmosphere. You ring doorbell 31 and are greeted by your host Igor Zincenco and his team, who go on to fully explain each well-balanced, satisfying dish which features on a modern surprise menu inspired by Hungarian classics. Do opt for one of the two well-chosen wine pairings.

Name: Neked Főztem
Description En: This inviting roadside pub sits in an elevated spot and is fronted by a pleasant terrace. Inside it’s warm and welcoming with a rustic feel – thanks to a log burner crackling away on colder nights. Its name translates as ‘I cooked for you’. The concise menu lists all things Hungarian and the friendly team are happy to talk you through it and offer suggestions. The gutsy home-cooking has plenty of flavour and can be paired with a selection of local wines.

Name: St. Andrea Restaurant
Description En: This stylish bar-cum-restaurant is owned by a small boutique winery and the creative dishes are designed to match their wines – some of which aren’t sold anywhere else in the world! The evening sees an à la carte menu that appeals to all, while during the day there’s a great value set lunch that’s a hit with the business community. Dishes are refined and well-presented, with a mix of local and international flavours; you might find salmon trout with blueberries and goat's cheese or Mangalitsa shoulder with butternut squash and peach. For the full experience, go for the 'Made in Hungary' chef’s menu.

Name: Botanica
Address: Hotel Botanica, Nyárfa utca 57, Dánszentmiklós, 2735, Hungary
Description En: Lovely gardens surround this delightful, family-owned country house, which comes with bespoke designer bedrooms and charming service. Start with a drink in one of the comfortable lounges before heading through to the elegant restaurant, where a spot on the terrace is a must in summer. The multi-course menu showcases refined, modern creations in dishes which pay tribute to the locality, as well as the chef’s Swabian roots. Both wine and non-alcoholic drinks pairings are on offer, along with fermented beverages crafted from local fruits and vegetables.

Name: KOLLÁZS
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace, Széchenyi István tér 5, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description En: The Four Seasons Gresham Palace hotel is a beautiful art nouveau building which was constructed in 1906 for the Gresham Life Assurance Company. Set in the heart of Budapest, directly opposite the Széchenyi Chain Bridge, its restaurant makes the perfect place to dine when visiting the city. The relaxed, cosy atmosphere is matched perfectly by a menu of familiar French brasserie classics, with a few Hungarian dishes thrown in. The steak tartare is made at the table, the roast chicken for two is carved in front of you and the rum baba is a hit.

Name: NOON
Address: Lua Resort, Anna Sétány 3, Balatonfüred, 8230, Hungary
Description En: An exclusive lakeside resort plays host to this elegant restaurant (if you’re not staying the night, then pre-booking is essential in high season). Grab a cocktail in the stylish bar before enjoying a carefully curated selection of contemporary Hungarian dishes which fuse tradition with inventive modern touches. Local wines are a feature, and the smooth service shows the team’s knowledge and care. If the chocolate and cherry dessert is on the menu, be sure to choose it.

Name: Costes Downtown
Address: Prestige Hotel, Vigyázó Ferenc utca 5, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description En: 2025 sees Costes Downtown celebrate its 10th anniversary. Located on the ground floor of the Prestige Hotel, this stylish restaurant features a striking interior with a living wall and ceiling that bring nature indoors. Ask for one of the cosy booths or book the chef’s table for a close-up view of the action in the open kitchen. The set-priced lunch and dinner menus are joined by a tasting option at dinner, with the visually impressive dishes seeing Hungarian favourites reinterpreted in an elaborate modern manner.

Name: Tihanyi Vinarius
Description En: Take in lovely views over the countryside and the lake from the terrace of this charming thatched building dating from 1822. The interior is full of historic character – it even boasts a hidden vaulted brick-built room which is used for private events – and the formal service suits the style of the place. Some unusual and rarely seen ingredients feature in well-crafted dishes; Tihany is famous for its lavender, so the ‘vinarius 200 tortaszelet’ dessert is a must.

Name: Teyföl
Description En: Owners Brigi and Bence have created what they feel is their perfect restaurant in Teyföl, whose name translates as ‘sour cream’ – an ingredient used frequently in Hungarian cuisine. The restaurant sits within a characterful period building on a narrow cobbled street in the Old Town, and its bright, modern bistro-style interior provides a complete contrast. Multiple flavours, textures and colours come together in classically based dishes with a well-restrained level of creativity, such as confit chicken pancakes or a gypsy-style roast.

Name: VIRTU
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
Description En: Located on the 28th floor of the tallest building in Budapest, the MOL Campus, VIRTU affords stunning views out over this historic city and the River Danube. Start with cocktails in the smart bar, then head through to the spacious, two-roomed restaurant. The menu offers something for everyone, with a pleasing mix of modern and classical dishes. If it’s available, the Keszthely sturgeon with orda cheese gnocchi and champagne sauce is delicious – and ensure you finish with the strikingly modern somlói trifle. A fine selection of wines and professional service from a caring team complete the picture.

Name: Stand25 Bisztró
Description En: There’s always a contented buzz to this neighbourhood bistro on the Buda side of the Danube. It’s owned by the same team as Stand, so their ethos around quality is the same, and you’ll be looked after by a slick team. Cooking focuses on Hungarian classics with a Mediterranean edge and, while dishes are hearty with robust flavours, they also have a refined edge.

Name: Rutin
Description En: Three hours pass in a flash at this intimate little restaurant, which is proudly run by a friendly couple. Dinner starts at 7pm, with Fanni welcoming guests and looking after their every need. Dávid, meanwhile, is behind the scenes preparing a very personalised multi-course set menu that combines classic Hungarian favourites with family recipes and his childhood memories. Dishes have a feel-good factor, from tarragon soup with charcoal-roasted Mangalitsa to sugar bread with ice cream, caramel and Tokaji jus – and Dávid tells their story to the room as he brings each one out of the kitchen or finishes it off tableside.

Name: Hoppá! Bistro
Description En: This contemporary eatery stands out amongst the myriad choices on vibrant Október Street, both for its smooth service and its modern, well-presented cooking – and it's certainly a popular spot. The menu sees traditional Hungarian recipes brought up-to-date, and there’s a range of daily specials and an excellent value lunch menu on offer too. You might find smoked catfish with onions and sesame seeds, followed by veal with bread dumplings and sage, then, for dessert, crème brûlée accompanied by seasonal fruit. Local beers and wines complete the picture.

Name: Onyx
Description En: Pinpointing the Onyx experience can be a challenging task, as this is a place that undergoes constant evolution in the pursuit of self-improvement. What can be said, is that you will be part of a truly immersive experience, as you arrive at the same time as your fellow guests, ready to share a memorable evening together. The communal experience is a stimulating, sensory and provocative one, that uses a multi-course tasting menu to showcase the development of food in the past, present and future. Without giving too much away, your night here will include light, sound, capes and contemplation!

Name: Nobu Budapest
Address: Kempinski Hotel Corvinus Budapest, Erzsébet tér 7-8, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description En: Wherever you hail from, there’s a high chance you’ll have heard of Nobu, as the group’s restaurants now span the globe. At the Budapest branch – which sits inside a chic hotel – you’ll find a stylish, minimalist aesthetic that takes in wooden tables, fretwork screens and Japanese lanterns. The extensive menu follows the usual Nobu format, with a wide range of sushi and both hot and cold Nobu classics (such as miso black cod or yellowtail tartare with caviar), and there’s also a section dedicated to Wagyu beef. Bento boxes are available at lunch and there’s an omakase on offer for the undecided.

Name: Lokal at the Lake
Description En: It’s all in the name. Set in a small village on the southern banks of Lake Balaton, just a stone’s throw from the water, this intimate bistro follows a purely local ethos. From the fixtures and fittings to the furnishings and the food, everything you see has been produced in the region. The rustic small plates have a fittingly traditional Hungarian heart and come with bold flavours – you might find green pea soup with goat’s cheese and mint, followed by rabbit with vegetable sauce and bread pudding. Choose four per person or opt for the excellent value Chef’s Menu of current kitchen favourites.

Name: Zazie Bistro
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
Description En: Zazie Bistro sits within the tallest skyscraper in Budapest, the MOL Campus, and offers some great views out over the city. It’s a spacious place that incorporates a large open restaurant, a terrace and even a café. The chef brings with him plenty of experience, which shines through in the well-executed, classically inspired, rustic dishes. These could include chilled fruit soups in the summer, or a top-class schnitzel with deliciously creamy potato salad – with the potatoes supplied by the chef’s brother-in-law. There’s also a great value business lunch on offer.

Name: Villa Kabala
Description En: Perched high up the hillside in the Badacsony region, with far reaching views of Lake Balaton, this period villa was once home to artist István Farkas. Now under the ownership of an ambitious and enthusiastic couple, the team here are establishing it as something of a destination restaurant. A concise lunch offering is followed by a well-balanced tasting menu – you won’t get much more local than this, with the cheese, salami, sausages, beers and wines all family made. They even have their own coffee roaster and pottery workshop too. Book a bedroom with a terrace and look forward to a fantastic breakfast.

Name: IKON
Description En: Set on a main street in the heart of the city, IKON stands out among the other eateries for its smart look, structured service and confident cooking. The chef spent time working in England and his dishes are an intriguing mix of reworked Hungarian classics and some British influences – go for something from the ‘Traditions Reborn’ section and be sure not to miss dessert. For a more immersive experience, book the chic Kitchen Table.

Name: FELIX Kitchen & Bar
Description En: FELIX Kitchen & Bar sits behind the breathtaking neo-renaissance façade of the Várkert Kioszk, a building whose original function was to pump water to the Royal Palace. Today, along with a gallery, it’s now home to this plush restaurant boasting a stunningly restored ceiling and an air-conditioned terrace. While maintaining a certain air of elegance that’s suited to the historic building, it takes on something of a Mediterranean vibe, serving an extensive range of dishes that covers everything from carpaccios and risottos to mezze plates and lobster to share.

Name: GÓRÉ
Description En: A góré is a barn used to dry cereals, and that was this sleek restaurant’s former function – although it's hard to imagine that following its chic refurbishment. Climb the stairs to the raised dining area beneath the beams to enjoy the view out through the floor-to-ceiling windows; alternatively, enjoy an al fresco experience on the covered terrace. The heart of the menu has strong classical foundations, but unique additions offer innovation and originality, with fermentation techniques featuring highly. The restaurant is remotely set in a sleepy village, so the comfy bedrooms are a real bonus.

Name: Tati
Description En: The owners of this restaurant in up-and-coming District 7 also have a farm in Biatorbágy, on the outskirts of the city, where they grow their own fruit and veg. Menus comprise a mix of meat, fish and plant-based combinations, and the use of traditional Hungarian recipes results in hearty, wholesome cooking. There’s a natural feel to both the appearance and the flavour of the dishes, as well as to the accompanying natural, biodynamic and organic wines, which are sourced from vineyards in close proximity to the city.

Name: Talu
Address: Andrássy Kúria & Spa, Fő út 94, Tarcal, 3915, Hungary
Description En: The Andrássy Kúria & Spa hotel sits within a 200-year-old manor house once used as a hunting lodge by the Andrássy family, and the warmly run talu restaurant occupies its impressive vaulted cellar – as well as spilling out onto its terrace in the warmer months. The chef reinterprets traditional regional and family recipes to create modern versions of old favourites, with Hungarian produce such as Mangalitsa pork kept to the fore. Local Tokaj wines are also a draw, with many available by the glass; a stay one of their bedrooms provides the perfect excuse to sample more than one!

Name: Horgonyzó Kisvendéglő
Description En: Simplicity leads the way at this endearing restaurant set just a short stroll from the River Tisza. The room has an unfussy lodge style and there’s plenty of outdoor space courtesy of both a front and rear terrace. Cooking is fresh and well-executed, and offers something for everyone, from Hungarian classics to pizzas, burgers and street food. The wood-fired oven plays a key role, and everything is prepared with love and care.

Name: A Konyhám Stúdió 365
Description En: Take the lift to the 3rd floor of the Balaton Üzletház shopping mall and you’ll find this bright restaurant with a smart interior and a partial view over the lake. Chef and well-known personality, Gabriella Szikra – kitted out in her trademark cap – has a genuine desire to please, and her modern Hungarian dishes come with bold flavours and arty presentation. Be sure to go for the excellent local wine pairings.

Name: 67 Sigma Restaurant
Description En: Start with a stroll around the pretty Old Town, then head to this historic property tucked away on a cobbled street; you enter via an enclosed courtyard and terrace, into a smart restaurant with plenty of atmosphere. Good quality produce is used to create fresh, flavoursome Hungarian dishes in a modern style. Courteous service comes from a local team.

Name: MoszkvaTéЯ Bisztró
Address: Monastery Boutique Hotel, Fő utca 30, Budapest, 1011, Hungary
Description En: The younger sibling of Arany Kaviár sits on the ground floor of a characterful hotel that was once a monastery. The cuisine here, too, has a Russian theme, with plenty of favourites such as chicken Kiev and some delicious pelmeni (dumplings). The young team are bright and friendly, and a concise list of Hungarian wines completes the picture.

Name: Avalon Ristorante
Address: H3519 Miskolctapolca, Iglói utca 15, Miskolc, 3519, Hungary
Description En: Expectation builds as you follow the winding road that leads up to the Avalon Resort & SPA hotel in the Bükk Mountains. A village unto itself, it’s a family friendly place – and the restaurant’s menu reflects this. There’s something for everyone here, from pizzas and pastas to Wagyu cooked on the Josper grill, while the wine list offers a great selection to accompany your meal. Sit in the stylish bar beside the open kitchen or head through further into the conservatory.

Name: Textúra
Description En: Set almost opposite its sister restaurant, Borkonyha Winekitchen, is this stylish, design-led brasserie with a relaxed atmosphere, a living wall of moss and a central wooden ‘tree’. Seasonally led dishes are ambitious and creative, and there are some real gems from Hungary on the wine list.
